First, let's factor out ${t}^{5}$ from the expression:

$$
49{t}^{9}+36{t}^{5}={t}^{5}\,(49{t}^{4}+36).
$$

Now focus on factoring $(49{t}^{4}+36).$  

To factor a sum of squares, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using ${i}^{2}=-1.$ Finally, we factor it as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}49{t}^{4}+36 & =49{t}^{4}-(-36) \\  & =49{t}^{4}-(36{i}^{2}) \\  & =(7{t}^{2})^{2}-(6i)^{2} \\  & =(7{t}^{2}+6i)(7{t}^{2}-6i).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting back, we obtain

$$
{t}^{5}\,(49{t}^{4}+36)={t}^{5}(7{t}^{2}+6i)(7{t}^{2}-6i).
$$
